title: Streaming schema drift detector and decoder mirroring experiment
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Objective: Validate and harden JSON mode behavior when streaming responses interleave partial JSON objects with tool/function-calls, and measure how constrained-decoder fallbacks behave under real traffic patterns. We will mirror a sampled subset of production traffic into a canary constrained-decoder instance, run a drift detector across streaming fragments, and implement automated rollback triggers when schema adherence drops below threshold.

Scope:
- Build a streaming-schema-drift detector that operates on incremental token streams (partial JSON fragments), flags syntactic breaks and semantic field omission relative to a target schema, and reports time-aligned alarms.
- Deploy a traffic-mirroring pipeline from API edge to a canary constrained-decoder variant that runs with stricter temperature/penalty constraints and schema-enforcement wrapper. Mirrored requests must include metadata (prompt hash, model variant, route) and avoid PII landing in canary logs.
- Warmup KV cache heuristics for mirrored workload to avoid artificial latency-related degradation.
- Implement a fallback policy prototype: when canary decoder shows >2% schema-error rate over rolling 5m window or error spike >0.5%/minute, create alert and tag route for automated traffic steering to primary relaxed-decoder until fix is confirmed.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Detector reports true positive rate >= 92% on labeled synthetically-mangled stream dataset and false positive rate <= 1.5% on clean dataset.
2) Traffic mirroring can handle 5% of peak route RPS with <=1% additional latency to the primary path (mirroring async).
3) Canary constrained-decoder runs with KV-cache warmup and shows representative latency distribution; documented comparison on console dashboards (per-route histogram).
4) Runbook documented for incident response and automated rollback policy implemented as prototype (canary tag + alerting).

Deliverables/Artifacts:
- Prototype detector service and CLI (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-drifts/compare)
- Helm manifest + canary constrained-decoder deployment (k8s charts in infra repo)
- Dashboard: console redirects to /dashboards/stream-schema-drift (temporary)
- Runbook: Confluence page (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Streaming+Schema+Drift+Runbook)
- Tests: fuzz corpus + labeled mangling fixtures (s3://redwood-test-fixtures/streaming-schema-mangle)

Risks and notes:
- Privacy: mirrored requests must be scrubbed. Work with Security to add a redaction step; do not log full PII to canary.
- Race conditions: partial JSON fragments may appear valid until final tokens; detector must operate incrementally and support retraction/repair signals.
- Metrics inflation: metric backfills from mirrored runs must be flagged so they do not impact billing/SLAs.

Next steps:
- Pair with infra to wire traffic mirroring (blk: infra-ticket).
- Land initial detector prototype and synthetic test suite.
- Run 72-hour mirror run for two representative routes and evaluate.
